title: Command pack (Command line tool)
description: Commands for the typed command drill. One launch pack per unit (unit-04.json). The extra set is a pack of its own (unit-04-extra.json) marked "set": "extra". The shape is frozen in docs/COMMAND-LINE-PLAN.md section 4. The page ignores a field it does not know, and the content check warns about one.

id.description: Pack id, e.g. unit-04 (the extra set: unit-04-extra).

title.description: Unit title, e.g. Unit 4.0 Configuring Network Addressing.

set.description: Only on a pack of extra commands, which students opt in to. A launch pack has no "set". The loader stamps it on each command of the pack.

reviewed.description: Set true once the teacher has read the pack.

placeholder.description: true = test content that must be deleted and replaced. The site shows a Test content banner and the content check keeps warning. Never set this on real content.

lastCommand.description: Kept by the content kit (assemble.ps1 -CommandsOnly): the highest command number this pack has ever used, 9 for n-u04-c009, so a dropped id is never used again when the pack is rebuilt. The page and the content check ignore it.

lastVersion.description: The same for version numbers (10 for n-u04-v010). The page and the content check ignore it.

source.description: Key from the exam's "sources" in data/exams.json, e.g. certmaster.

section.description: Reading section that teaches the command, e.g. 4.4.1.

quote.description: The one or two sentences from the reading (40 words max). May be empty.

find.description: Teacher helper: three to six words to search for in the section to locate the quote. Never shown to students.

origin.description: Present exactly when no id in "typedFormOf" is a question: a flashcard's command, a command Mr. Flauto names, or an extra command. It names the one source item the command is modeled on. A command that types a published question has no origin of its own.

verbatim.description: true = copied word for word. Only allowed in lab-only (private) packs.

lines.description: Right lines that print the same output, 36 characters at most. Plain text the way the reading or the objectives print them. No patterns and no second spellings: how a line may be typed is decided in code.

sections.description: Optional, read only by the content kit: the reading section that teaches these lines when it is not the command's own reference section.

output.description: What one answer group prints in this version: a text, or the exhibit of the version's follow-up question. Never both.

text.description: Written fresh: at most 12 lines of at most 25 characters, lines separated by \n, no tabs, no em dashes. Empty ("") where the real command prints nothing.

exhibitOf.description: Print the exhibit of this version's own follow-up question in place of a text. The same id as followUp.question.

followUp.description: A question about the output, asked under it whichever right line was typed. For now always a published question. One written in place is refused by the content check.

question.description: Id of a published practice question of the same exam that reads this output, e.g. n-u04-q054.

id.description: Course code, unit, the letter v, a number: n-u04-v001. A saved drill remembers it. Never reuse one.

outputs.description: One output for each answer group, in the same order as "accept".

command.description: One command: a task, the lines that answer it, and what each prints. It needs "typedFormOf", "origin", or both. No weight is stored: the draw works it out from the partner question's source.

id.description: Course code, unit, the letter c, a number: n-u04-c001. Shared with no question, card, or version of any exam. Never reuse one.

status.description: Drafts are hidden from students (preview with ?drafts=1).

help.description: Only on a command with help off: there help, ?, and a command's own help (ipconfig /?) print Help off, as on some exam items. Left out, help is on. A content chat turns help off on the easiest commands, about a quarter of them, on the line under "id" (docs/CONTENT-GUIDE.md, "Help off").

typedFormOf.description: Always a list: the published questions, or the one flashcard, of this exam whose command line this command types. No question or card is the partner of two commands.

system.description: The system the task names. The prompt text is set in code.

task.description: One or two sentences that name the system and end by asking which command. It never holds an accepted line.

accept.description: One to three answer groups. A group holds lines only. Each group prints its own output.

alsoWorks.description: Optional: lines a real system would run for this job that the reading does not teach, such as ifconfig -a. A typed line that is one of them to the matcher costs no try, prints no output, and reads Not counted. In a real pack it starts empty and grows only from what the blind command check types. Never a second spelling of an accepted line.

versions.description: One to three versions of the output. The task and the accepted lines are the same in every version.
